title: `variance` and `stddev` are the sample's
description: DuckDB names both distributions: `var_samp` and `stddev_samp` divide by `count(x) - 1` (Bessel's correction), `var_pop` and `stddev_pop` by `count(x)`. `variance` is an alias of `var_samp` and `stddev` of `stddev_samp`.

The docs give these per function, without listing the argument types; the types here rest on the functions taking any numeric argument. The docs' formulas (`(sum(x^2) - sum(x)^2 / count(x)) / (count(x) - 1)`) define the result; the algorithm is Welford's (duckdb-var-stddev).

Round 2 (source): `variance` is an alias of `var_samp` and `stddev` of `stddev_samp` in the function list. Each of the four has one `DOUBLE` overload, so `BIGINT` and `DECIMAL` arguments are cast to `DOUBLE` first (duckdb-stat-arg-types); the distribution is the same for every argument type. `var_samp` divides by `count - 1` and is NULL for one value; `var_pop` divides by `count` and is 0 for one value.

Round 4 (probes): for BIGINT 1, 2, 4 `var_samp` is 7/3 and `var_pop` 14/9; for DECIMAL 1.5, 2.5, 4.0 `var_samp` is 1.5833… and `stddev_samp` its root. One value gives `var_samp` NULL and `var_pop` 0 for both types.
reference: Substrait's `variance` and `std_dev` take `distribution` (`SAMPLE`, `POPULATION`); sverify reads an omitted one as `SAMPLE` (`SubstraitLean/Options.lean`, `Parse.lean`), and the lift writes `VAR_SAMP`/`VAR_POP` (`sql_lift/_base.py`, `_distribution`). DuckDB's defaults agree.

provenance.notes: Read at tag v2.0.0 (commit d54cbbe3); the tests were not run. The tests pin the sample (n - 1) and population (n) divisors, `variance` = `var_samp` and `stddev` = `stddev_samp`. Their inputs are `INTEGER`, which binds the single `DOUBLE` overload through an exact cast, so they run the `DOUBLE` aggregate on exact doubles: they settle `fp64`. No test runs a `BIGINT` or `DECIMAL` argument; those stay at the source reading (one overload, so the same distribution).
